back_blocks.md: A **magnet** is an object with a **north pole** and a **south pole**. It attracts magnetic materials and can attract or repel other magnets.

back_blocks.md: A **magnetic material** is a material that is **attracted** to a magnet. It is attracted to **both poles** and can be **magnetised**.

cards.front_md: Define the term **magnetic material**.

back_blocks.md: A **non-magnetic material** is **neither attracted nor repelled** by a magnet.

cards.front_md: Define the term **non-magnetic material**.
cards.back_md: A **non-magnetic material** is **neither attracted nor repelled** by a magnet.

back_blocks.md: The magnetic metals are **iron**, **cobalt** and **nickel**. **Steel** is also magnetic because it is an alloy containing iron.

cards.front_md: Which metals are **magnetic**?
cards.back_md: The magnetic metals are **iron**, **cobalt** and **nickel**. **Steel** is also magnetic because it is an alloy containing iron.

front_blocks.md: How can you test whether an object is a **magnet**?

back_blocks.md: Bring the object close to a known magnet:

- It is a **magnet** if it is **repelled** by the known magnet
- It is a **magnetic material** if it is only ever **attracted**
- It is a **non-magnetic material** if it is neither attracted nor repelled

back_blocks.md: **Induced magnetism** is when a magnetic material **temporarily becomes a magnet** while it is inside a magnetic **field**.

cards.front_md: What is **induced magnetism**? **(Extended Tier Only)**
cards.back_md: **Induced magnetism** is when a magnetic material **temporarily becomes a magnet** while it is inside a magnetic **field**.

front_blocks.md: What happens to the ends of a magnetic material when magnetism is **induced** in it?

back_blocks.md: One end becomes a **north pole** and the other a **south pole**. The end **closest** to the magnet has the **opposite pole** to the magnet's nearest pole.

cards.front_md: What happens to the ends of a magnetic material when magnetism is **induced** in it?
cards.back_md: One end becomes a **north pole** and the other a **south pole**. The end **closest** to the magnet has the **opposite pole** to the magnet's nearest pole.

front_blocks.md: Induced magnets keep their magnetism after being removed from the magnetic field.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
An induced magnet **loses its magnetism quickly** when it is removed from the magnetic field.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

Induced magnets keep their magnetism after being removed from the magnetic field.
cards.back_md:
**False.**

An induced magnet **loses its magnetism quickly** when it is removed from the magnetic field.

front_blocks.md: Induced magnetism can cause a magnet to repel a magnetic material. **(Extended Tier Only)**

back_blocks.md: **False.**
Induced magnetism **always** causes a force of **attraction** between the magnet and the induced magnet.

cards.front_md:

cards.back_md:

back_blocks.md: A **permanent magnet** produces its **own magnetic field** and does not lose its magnetism easily. Permanent magnets are made from materials such as **steel**.

cards.front_md: Define the term **permanent magnet**.
cards.back_md: A **permanent magnet** produces its **own magnetic field** and does not lose its magnetism easily. Permanent magnets are made from materials such as **steel**.

front_blocks.md: Why is **steel** used for permanent magnets but **soft iron** used in electromagnets?

back_blocks.md: **Steel** stays magnetised for a long time, so it is used for **permanent magnets**. **Soft iron** loses its magnetism as soon as the cause of the induced magnetism is removed, so it is used in **electromagnets** and transformers.

cards.front_md: Why is **steel** used for permanent magnets but **soft iron** used in electromagnets?
cards.back_md: **Steel** stays magnetised for a long time, so it is used for **permanent magnets**. **Soft iron** loses its magnetism as soon as the cause of the induced magnetism is removed, so it is used in **electromagnets** and transformers.

front_blocks.md: An **electromagnet** is made by winding coils of wire around a **______** core.

back_blocks.md: An **electromagnet** is made by winding coils of wire around a **soft iron** core.

cards.front_md: An **electromagnet** is made by winding coils of wire around a **______** core.
cards.back_md: An **electromagnet** is made by winding coils of wire around a **soft iron** core.

front_blocks.md: An electromagnet can be switched on and off.

back_blocks.md: **True.**
The electromagnet is switched **on** when **current** flows through the coils and switched **off** when no current flows.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

An electromagnet can be switched on and off.
cards.back_md:
**True.**

The electromagnet is switched **on** when **current** flows through the coils and switched **off** when no current flows.

front_blocks.md: State three ways to increase the strength of an **electromagnet**.

back_blocks.md: The strength of an electromagnet can be increased by:

- Increasing the **current**
- Increasing the **number of turns** of the coil
- Adding a **soft iron core**

cards.front_md: State three ways to increase the strength of an **electromagnet**.
cards.back_md:

- Adding a **soft iron core**

front_blocks.md: The strength of a permanent magnet can be changed.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
It is not possible to change the strength of a **permanent magnet**. Only an **electromagnet's** strength can be changed.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

front_blocks.md: Define the term **magnetic field**. **(Extended Tier Only)**

back_blocks.md: A **magnetic field** is a region in which a **magnetic pole** experiences a **force**.

cards.front_md: Define the term **magnetic field**. **(Extended Tier Only)**
cards.back_md: A **magnetic field** is a region in which a **magnetic pole** experiences a **force**.

front_blocks.md: How is the direction of a magnetic field at a point defined? **(Extended Tier Only)**

back_blocks.md: The direction of a magnetic field at a point is the direction of the **force** on the **north pole** of a magnet at that point.

cards.front_md: How is the direction of a magnetic field at a point defined? **(Extended Tier Only)**
cards.back_md: The direction of a magnetic field at a point is the direction of the **force** on the **north pole** of a magnet at that point.

front_blocks.md: What are magnetic **field lines**? **(Extended Tier Only)**

back_blocks.md: **Field lines** are lines drawn around a magnet to represent its magnetic field. Each line has an **arrow** showing the **direction** of the field.

cards.front_md: What are magnetic **field lines**? **(Extended Tier Only)**
cards.back_md: **Field lines** are lines drawn around a magnet to represent its magnetic field. Each line has an **arrow** showing the **direction** of the field.

front_blocks.md: In which direction do magnetic field lines go? **(Extended Tier Only)**

back_blocks.md: Magnetic field lines always go **from** a **north** pole **to** a **south** pole.

cards.front_md: In which direction do magnetic field lines go? **(Extended Tier Only)**
cards.back_md: Magnetic field lines always go **from** a **north** pole **to** a **south** pole.

front_blocks.md: The magnetic field is strongest at the poles of a bar magnet. **(Extended Tier Only)**

back_blocks.md: **True.**
The magnetic field is **strongest at the poles**, where the field lines are **closest together**.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

The magnetic field is strongest at the poles of a bar magnet. **(Extended Tier Only)**
cards.back_md:
**True.**

The magnetic field is **strongest at the poles**, where the field lines are **closest together**.

front_blocks.md: How is the weakening of a bar magnet's field with distance shown by its field lines? **(Extended Tier Only)**

back_blocks.md: The magnetic field becomes **weaker** as the distance from the magnet increases, so the field lines get **further apart**.
